candidates.name: Thames Barrier
candidates.story: Engineers used gates that rotate up from the riverbed to block storm surges while leaving navigation spans clear when open. The barrier became operational in 1982 and officially opened in 1984.
candidates.art_direction: Show a raised steel gate between two of the silver piers from a low river viewpoint so the gate profile is visible.

candidates.name: Falkirk Wheel
candidates.story: The rotating boat lift used segmented arms with high-strength friction-grip bolted site joints. The joint design accommodated transport and the fatigue from repeated rotation. The completed lift opened in 2002.
candidates.art_direction: Show the wheel under assembly beside the aqueduct, with a crane lifting an arm segment into position and a visible bolted flange joint. Use contractor and engineering records to establish the erection sequence and the opposed arms and gondola-ring geometry.

candidates.name: Brunelleschi’s Dome
candidates.story: Brunelleschi raised Florence Cathedral’s double-shell octagonal dome without full wooden centering. Herringbone brickwork helped stabilize the increasingly inclined courses while successive closed rings held the structure in equilibrium. The dome body was completed on 30 August 1436; the lantern was added later, after Brunelleschi died in 1446.
candidates.art_direction: Show the dome body under construction in the early 1430s, without the later lantern. Use an elevated view of the octagonal drum and rising double shells, eight principal ribs and an open crown. A near working edge should clearly expose vertical bricks interrupting inclined horizontal courses in the herringbone pattern. Include modest work platforms at height, not huge wooden centering filling the cathedral. Research period hoists separately before drawing machinery; avoid modern cranes. Compose landscape and portrait independently with quiet upper-right space; keep brick orientation legible in grayscale. The construction angle is masonry stability, not the finished Florence skyline.
